# PS5 HD Camera for PC

> A free, open-source (GPL-3.0) driver that makes the PlayStation 5 HD Camera (model CFI-ZEY1) a regular webcam on a PC: native 1920x1080 at 60 fps and background blur (bokeh) from real stereo depth computed on the GPU, on Windows 11, with Linux (bokeh experimental, Vulkan) and macOS (no bokeh) support.

Key facts:

- Hardware: only the PlayStation 5 HD Camera (CFI-ZEY1). It plugs into a regular USB 3 port; no adapter is needed. On USB 2.0 it only delivers 640x400. The PS4 camera is not supported.
- Windows 11: the camera appears as "PS5 Camera" in Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Discord, Telegram, OBS Studio, browsers and the Camera app (Media Foundation, WinRT, DirectShow). Install: download PS5CameraDriver.msi (English) or PS5CameraDriver-ru.msi (Russian) from https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver/releases/latest and run it; unattended: `msiexec /i PS5CameraDriver.msi /qn BOKEH=on|off`. A winget package `KROU4.PS5CameraDriver` is under review.
- Bokeh without neural networks: depth from the camera's two sensors (census transform + semi-global matching) in Direct3D 11 shaders; the whole head stays sharp (silhouette from depth), exposure is metered on the person, motion-compensated noise reduction and automatic anti-flicker help in dim rooms. It is switched like Windows' own camera effects: Settings → Bluetooth & devices → Cameras → PS5 Camera → Camera effects.
- How it works on Windows: no kernel code and no test mode. A service uploads the camera firmware through Windows' built-in WinUSB; the camera then re-connects as a standard UVC camera; a Device MFT inside Windows Camera Frame Server does the GPU processing.
- Firmware: the camera needs firmware every time it is plugged in. Sony's firmware is not redistributed: the installer downloads the original image from public copies, checks its SHA-256 and applies a 90-byte patch (1080p at 60 fps, a depth mode, automatic exposure). Without internet access the installation still completes and the service fetches the firmware later.
- Performance (RTX 3060 Ti, 1920x1080 at 60 fps): 2.6–2.9 ms GPU time per frame without effects, 8.6–9.0 ms with bokeh; about 60 MB / 100–130 MB of GPU memory. A GPU with Direct3D 11 (Vulkan 1.1 on Linux) is required.
- Linux: `sudo bash install.sh` from PS5CameraDriver-linux.zip (systemd and udev required); `--bokeh on` adds the experimental bokeh (x86_64, Vulkan 1.1, v4l2loopback camera "PS5 Camera").
- macOS: `sudo bash install.sh` from PS5CameraDriver-macos.zip (Command Line Tools required); 1080p at 30/60 fps without bokeh.
- Limitations: one program uses the camera at a time; depth is measured from about half a metre.
- Not affiliated with Sony Interactive Entertainment. PlayStation and PS5 are trademarks of Sony Interactive Entertainment Inc.

## Docs

- [Website (English)](https://krou4.github.io/PS5CameraDriver/): overview, install, performance, FAQ
- [Website (Russian)](https://krou4.github.io/PS5CameraDriver/ru/): the same in Russian
- [README](https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver/blob/main/README.md): full description, firmware patch, architecture, building from source
- [Windows install and troubleshooting](https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver/blob/main/installer/README.txt): modes, settings, ps5cam-ctl commands
- [Linux install](https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver/blob/main/installer/linux/README.txt): plain camera and Vulkan bokeh

## Downloads

- [Latest release](https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver/releases/latest): MSI and ZIP for Windows, Linux and macOS packages
- [Source code](https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver): GPL-3.0

## Optional

- [Firmware patch](https://github.com/KROU4/PS5CameraDriver/blob/main/firmware/ps5cam-firmware.json): the original firmware hash, its public sources and the byte changes
